papers.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
papers.summary: Gradient-boosted trees infer buoyancy-glitch parameters from global properties of 12,580 synthetic low-luminosity red giants, accurately recovering location and width but not amplitude.

papers.title: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
papers.summary: Simulation-based inference with a diffusion/flow-matching transformer separates LISA stochastic components, matching MCMC posteriors and remaining robust to glitches, gaps, and varying noise.

papers.title: Characterising stellar photometry with invertible neural networks: Joint inference of stellar parameters and extinction
papers.comment: 27 pages, 14 figures, 1 table, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.summary: Conditional invertible neural networks jointly infer stellar parameters and extinction from Gaia+2MASS photometry, matching extinction structures but overestimating values by 0.5–0.7 mag.

papers.title: Fast and accurate large-volume Lyman-$\alpha$ forest mocks with three-dimensional U-Net trained on IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO
papers.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables, submitted to JCAP. Comments are welcome
papers.summary: A 3D U-Net emulates Lyman-alpha forest flux from density and velocity fields, reproducing TNG and FLAMINGO statistics in large-volume mocks.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement of Amortized Bayesian Inference Across Physics
papers.summary: An AI agent recursively designs amortized Bayesian inference networks for six physics fields, returning accurate posteriors for real observations after likelihood reweighting.

papers.title: Kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich Velocity Reconstruction Using Vision Transformers
papers.comment: 15 pages, 13 figures. Accepted to the New in Machine Learning (NewInML) workshop at NeurIPS 2026
papers.summary: Vision Transformers reconstruct kSZ velocity fields from CMB and large-scale structure maps, improving fidelity over quadratic estimators in a single simulation.

papers.title: Machine learning reveals new Galactic C-rich and O-rich AGB sources
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 30 pages, 24 figures, 5 tables
papers.summary: XGBoost classifies Gaia DR3 AGB candidates into 304,090 O-rich and 4,227 C-rich stars, revealing distinct spatial and vertical Milky Way distributions.
